purpose: Minimize wasted Google Flow credits by requiring asset-grounded preflight, continuity checks, and low-risk validation before paid/high-cost video generation.

promptTemplate.subject: who/what appears; bind to persona/ingredient asset ids
promptTemplate.environment: location/background from approved asset or explicit description
promptTemplate.style: approved style reference or template id
promptTemplate.continuity: what must remain identical to previous clip
promptTemplate.transition: how start frame moves toward end frame
promptTemplate.avoid: identity drift, object mutation, extra fingers/limbs, text artifacts, camera discontinuity, abrupt pose jumps

personaRules: Use one canonical persona asset pack per project unless the variant explicitly requests a different persona.
Lock face, hair, clothing, body proportions, key props and style references before first video generation.
Reuse project ingredients or named project assets instead of re-describing identity from text alone.
Store approved persona images, reference frames and asset ids in central registry and task payload.
continuityBridge: Save previous clip final frame as an image.
Use that saved frame as next clip start frame when continuity matters.
Where a planned endpoint is known, create or approve an explicit end-frame image before generation.
Describe only the motion/transition between the locked frames; do not re-invent subject identity.
After generation compare first/last frames, persona identity, object positions and camera direction with the storyboard contract.
creditGuard: Do not generate video from text-only when persona/reference assets can be prepared first.
Default outputCount to 1 for validation passes.
Use lower-cost supported model/generation for prompt validation before high-cost Quality generation when final quality does not yet need to be judged.
Do not request multiple variants until the base prompt and continuity bridge pass.
Do not regenerate to fix a problem that can be corrected in prompt, ingredient, frame or asset selection first.
Record credits/model/generation count per attempt and calculate waste caused by failed attempts.
completionRule: FLOW generation is not COMPLETE until result readback, purpose-fit audit, continuity audit and credit-efficiency review are recorded.
